meta.title: Tom's Bike Wash
meta.textType: story: a holiday job at home

paragraphs: On Saturday, April third, Tom started his first holiday job at eight o'clock. He washed bikes in the front garden for thirty baht a bike. Lily held up her hand-painted sign with the price, and Ben came to help with the hose. A blue bucket, a yellow sponge, and a brush stood beside Tom's red bike. Tom washed his own bike first, so the customers could see a clean one. Pip sat near the gate and watched the road. Two hours passed, and no customer came. Lily whispered to Ben, "Tom says that he is not nervous." "But he looks at the gate every minute," said Ben. "Does it bother you, Tom?" he asked. "No, I'm fine," said Tom.

Then a woman in a straw hat came to the gate with a small blue bike. "Is this the bike wash?" she asked. "My son got this bike recently, and it is already very dirty." "Yes, it is," said Tom, and he smiled. First, Ben sprayed the bike with water. Next, Tom washed it with the sponge. Then he cleaned the wheels with the brush. After that, Ben sprayed the soap away. Finally, Tom dried the bike with a cloth. "Thirty baht, please," said Tom. "Here you are," said the woman, and she paid him.

Suddenly, Pip picked up the yellow sponge and ran across the grass. "Stop, Pip!" shouted Tom, and he ran after him. Ben ran after them, too. Lily sat down on the porch step and laughed. When Tom bent down to catch Pip, a folded paper stuck out of his shirt pocket. Lily saw a picture of football boots and the price, eight hundred baht. Tom took the sponge from Pip's mouth. Then he pushed the paper deep into his pocket.

After that, the neighbors came one after another. A boy brought a gray bike, and a girl brought a pink one. Another boy brought a green one. "Do you sell bike bells?" asked the girl. "No, I only wash bikes," said Tom. Next came a man with two old bikes. "Can I have a discount for the second bike?" he asked. "The price is the same for every bike," said Tom, "but I will wash yours very well." The man laughed and paid sixty baht. Tom delivered each clean bike to its door. "Tom is a good worker," Ben told Lily, and she nodded.

At noon, Tom washed the sixth bike. Then he sat on the grass and counted the money in the tin. "One hundred and eighty baht," he said. "I will save every one." Lily looked at the paper in his pocket. She said nothing, and she gave him a glass of water. Tom drank it and looked at her. Pip lay down next to the tin with the yellow sponge.
